summary: Frontend-only retest of /construction.html against the 6 issues from iteration_17. All 6 previously reported defects are FIXED and verified on the public preview URL. Coverage: pinned .cx-seq-copy fit + active-step visibility at 1920x1080 / 1920x800 / 1600x760 / 1440x900 / 1280x720 across 6 scroll progress points for all 5 sequences (02/03/05/08/09); section-12 lead colour; section-06 6 data-pin groups + pin<->group lighting and toggle; prefers-reduced-motion stroke visibility; section-09 --dx explode transforms; section-07 log-index click->is-on mapping; hero label/opacity progression and header-overlap at 1280x720 and 1024x768; static un-pinned chapters at 1024x768 / 768x1024 / 390x844; header transparency over hero vs solid over sections 04/07/10/12/13; side menu CONSTRUCTION/DESIGN from both index.html and construction.html. Zero console/page errors on load and during scroll in every run. No source files modified.
critical_code_review_comments: construction.js: `const stepped = window.innerWidth > 1200` is evaluated once at load, so a desktop->tablet resize (or tablet->desktop) leaves the sequences in the wrong mode until reload. Not user-blocking for the tested breakpoints but a ScrollTrigger.matchMedia() would be more robust.

construction.css: the dark-context colour override for .cx-lead is still duplicated per wrapper (.cx-hero-copy, .cx-xfade-copy, .cx-final-copy, .cx-sec--dark). A single shared dark-context class would prevent the class of contrast bug fixed in section 12 from recurring on the next dark section added.

rca_of_the_issue: Not applicable - all previously reported root causes were addressed: vh-aware type scaling plus the <=1200px static-chapter media query removed the pinned-overflow; an explicit .cx-xfade-copy .cx-lead light colour fixed the section-12 contrast; real <g data-pin> groups plus the light() helper wired the pin->drawing link; inline strokeDashoffset='0' in the reduced-motion branch bypassed the Chromium style-invalidation issue; .cx-part[data-dx].is-lit{transform:translateX(var(--dx))} activated the explode; and moving the log-entry ScrollTrigger to 'top 30%'/'bottom 30%' aligned the highlight with the -160px click offset.
